caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:ac-3
attempts.entry_title: Coordinated neuronal ensembles in rat auditory cortex columns (See et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: Several main findings held up in this data: the number of coordinated neuronal ensembles (cNEs) grows with the number of units, members lie within 200 um of each other with no depth bias, cNE receptive fields are stronger than their members', and stimulus-driven models give fewer cNEs. The cNEs found are smaller (4.6 against 7.4 members), likely because the paper does not say how membership thresholds were set. The sharpness of pairwise synchrony, the best time bin and the higher information of cNE receptive fields did not reproduce, resting on settings the paper does not give. Persistence across spontaneous and evoked activity and the repeated-trial analyses could not be tested, as those recordings are not in the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of See, Atencio, Sohal and Schreiner (2018) on CRCNS ac-3, which holds the 16 columnar recordings (655 units) made with the 10-min DMR and RN stimuli, and the stimuli. It detects coordinated neuronal ensembles (cNEs) by PCA and ICA and tests their number, size, membership, depth, stability, pairwise correlation functions, bin size dependence, STRFs, and comparison with surrogate models. The 5-s repeats, the 15 repeats of the 10-min RN and the 64-channel recordings are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing See et al. (2018) from CRCNS ac-3

outcomes.statement: Across all penetrations, the sharpness and peak delay of pairwise correlation (PWC) functions covaried with the pairs' spike train correlation coefficients, accounting for about 50% of the variance.
outcomes.source: Results, Heterogeneous functional connectivity between columnar AI neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 2B to D
outcomes.quote: Across all penetrations, PWCs were fairly heterogeneous but sharpness and delay covaried with correlation coefficients, accounting for ~50% of the variance
outcomes.notes: R2 of sharpness and of peak delay on the 10-ms correlation coefficient over 14174 pairs are 0.133 and 0.114 (+-50 ms, linear axes; given as measured), 0.157 and 0.184 (log), 0.178 and 0.100 (+-100 ms, linear) and 0.234 and 0.249 (log). No reading comes near 0.5 +/- 0.05. Both measures fall as the correlation rises, as in the paper. Sharpness variants the claims file does not name (a baseline subtracted, from the two rates or from the outer lags, or windows of +-10 and +-20 ms) give sharpness R2 of 0.016 to 0.551; only the +-100 ms PWC with the outer-lag mean subtracted, on log axes, comes near 0.5 (0.551), with a delay R2 of 0.249 under the same lags.
deviations: PWC lag bins of 1 ms over +-50 and +-100 ms, the claims file's readings; the paper does not fix them.
PWCs use the spikes inside the stimulus period, on the stimulus clock, as the correlation coefficient does.

outcomes.statement: The correlation between the pairwise synchrony measures (sharpness, peak delay, correlation coefficient) and the distance between the pair's channels explained only about 10 to 30% of the variance.
outcomes.source: Results, Heterogeneous functional connectivity between columnar AI neurons, paragraph 3; Figure 2E to G
outcomes.quote: We observed similar trends in columnar recordings, although the correlation between these synchrony aspects and pairwise distance only explained ~10–30% of the total variance
outcomes.notes: Under both distances (depth difference, Euclidean distance on the probe) and both lag ranges, R2 is 0.005 to 0.055 for sharpness and delay and 0.032 to 0.037 for the correlation coefficient. None is in 0.09 to 0.33. Distance explains even less than the paper says. The measured value is the largest of the three R2 under the first reading (depth difference, +-50 ms).
deviations: PWC lag bins of 1 ms over +-50 and +-100 ms, the claims file's readings; the paper does not fix them.
PWCs use the spikes inside the stimulus period, on the stimulus clock, as the correlation coefficient does.

outcomes.statement: In an example columnar recording with 38 isolated neurons, the cNE detection found nine cNEs, with 2 to 6 member neurons each.
outcomes.source: Results, Identification of coordinated neuronal ensembles (cNEs), paragraph 2; Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: Applying this cNE detection algorithm to an actual AI columnar recording with 38 isolated neurons ( Figure 4D ), we identified nine separate cNEs ( Figure 4B ) with significantly contributing members ranging from 2 to 6 neurons
outcomes.notes: Site 10 is the only recording with 38 units. The detection finds 9 cNEs with 2 to 6 members (sign reading a), the same with five other seeds; under reading (b) the sizes are 2 to 5.
deviations: cNE detection details the paper does not fix are this attempt's readings, from the claims file's opening comment and cne.py (Marcenko-Pastur bound (1 + sqrt(n/T))^2, symmetric fastICA with logcosh, sign reading (a) for membership, spikes inside the stimulus period only).

outcomes.statement: cNEs detected independently in two interleaved halves of a recording were the same, with about 96% of the ICs of one half having a significant match in the other.
outcomes.source: Results, Identification of coordinated neuronal ensembles (cNEs), paragraph 4; Figure 4-figure supplement 2
outcomes.quote: Approximately 96% of independent components had significant matches ( Figure 4-figure supplement 2D and E ), indicating that the two interleaved parts of the recording contained the same independent components
outcomes.notes: 192 of 205 ICs of the two interleaved halves (93.7%) have a match above the 99th percentile of the null, under both null readings (a, shuffled against shuffled; b, real against shuffled); per recording 81 to 100%.
deviations: cNE detection details the paper does not fix are this attempt's readings, from the claims file's opening comment and cne.py (Marcenko-Pastur bound (1 + sqrt(n/T))^2, symmetric fastICA with logcosh, sign reading (a) for membership, spikes inside the stimulus period only).
Units without spikes in a half are left out of that half's detection and given weight 0 when the ICs are correlated (none in this data set at 10 ms).

outcomes.statement: cNEs detected in the first half of a recording predicted cNE activity in the second half; of 102 training cNEs, about 83% had significant matches to test cNE activity.
outcomes.source: Results, Identification of coordinated neuronal ensembles (cNEs), paragraph 5; Figure 4-figure supplement 3E
outcomes.quote: Across all penetrations, approximately 83% of training cNE activity had significant matches to test cNE activity
outcomes.notes: There are 102 training cNEs, the paper's number, but 100 (98.0%, quadratic projection; given as measured) or 101 (99.0%, linear) match above the 95th percentile of the non-matched correlations (606 values that are neither a row nor a column maximum, legend C). With every non-row-maximum value as the null, 95.1% or 99.0%. The training cNEs predict the test half better than the paper reports; by the criterion, a correct count with an out-of-range percentage is not reproduced.
deviations: cNE detection details the paper does not fix are this attempt's readings, from the claims file's opening comment and cne.py (Marcenko-Pastur bound (1 + sqrt(n/T))^2, symmetric fastICA with logcosh, sign reading (a) for membership, spikes inside the stimulus period only).
The test half is z-scored on itself and both IC sets are projected onto it; units silent in either half would be left out (none here).

outcomes.statement: The mutual information between cNE STRFs and the stimulus peaked at bin sizes of about 10 to 15 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, cNE identity is dependent on time bin size, paragraph 2; Figure 5A
outcomes.quote: Receptive field information peaked at bin sizes of approximately 10–15 ms ( Figure 5A )
outcomes.notes: No reading puts the largest MI at 10 or 15 ms. With the 5000 largest 1-ms samples of the interpolated activity as events (event reading a), the mean and median MI rise with bin size and peak at 35 ms under both projections (mean 0.696 bits linear, 0.729 quadratic), nearly flat from 15 ms. With the 5000 largest local peaks (event reading b), MI is highest at 2 ms and falls with bin size. Under reading (a) the 5000 events of a cNE fall in a median of 2857 (linear) distinct bins at 2 ms and 230 at 50 ms, so that at large bins the events are runs of neighbouring samples. With the STRF estimated on the events of the other half of the stimulus (a check the paper does not describe), the mean MI is 0.086 to 0.209 of the in-sample mean under event reading (a) and 0.024 to 0.292 under (b), and it still does not peak at 10 or 15 ms; under (a) the mean peaks at 5 ms (linear; 0.075 bits against 0.072 to 0.073 at 8 to 15 ms) or 50 ms (quadratic), the median at 50 ms, and under (b) at 2 ms. Under (a) the 5000 events fall in a median of 2857 (linear) or 3358 (quadratic) distinct bins at 2 ms. The result rests on the STRF resolution and MI bins, which the paper does not give.
deviations: cNE detection details the paper does not fix are this attempt's readings, from the claims file's opening comment and cne.py (Marcenko-Pastur bound (1 + sqrt(n/T))^2, symmetric fastICA with logcosh, sign reading (a) for membership, spikes inside the stimulus period only).

STRFs are event- or spike-triggered averages on 5-ms stimulus bins with 20 lags (100 ms), an assumption taken from the data set's sample code by the first author (Codes.zip, create_stim_segments_from_stim_mat.m, 'for AI cells, and 5 ms bins, nlags = 20 is sufficient'); the paper gives no STRF parameters. MI projection bins (25 bins over -5 to 5 SD) are a standard choice.

Each cNE's 5000 events are taken as its 5000 largest 1-ms activity samples or local peaks, readings of 'a threshold such that each cNE had 5000 events' (Materials and methods, STRF mutual information).

outcomes.statement: The number of detected cNEs decreased as the bin size increased.
outcomes.source: Results, cNE identity is dependent on time bin size, paragraph 3; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: we found that as the spike train temporal bin size increased, the number of recovered cNEs decreased ( Figure 5B )
outcomes.notes: The mean number of cNEs over the 16 recordings falls from 11.06 at 2 ms to 3.75 at 50 ms, monotonically (Spearman rho -1.0); every recording has fewer at 50 than at 2 ms.
deviations: cNE detection details the paper does not fix are this attempt's readings, from the claims file's opening comment and cne.py (Marcenko-Pastur bound (1 + sqrt(n/T))^2, symmetric fastICA with logcosh, sign reading (a) for membership, spikes inside the stimulus period only).

outcomes.statement: The mean number of member neurons per cNE increased as the bin size increased.
outcomes.source: Results, cNE identity is dependent on time bin size, paragraph 3; Figure 5C
outcomes.quote: the number of member neurons in each cNE increased ( Figure 5C )
outcomes.notes: The mean of per-recording mean sizes rises from 3.88 at 2 ms to 5.11 at 50 ms (Spearman rho 0.952, p = 0.00026; sign reading a), with small dips at 8 and 20 ms; under reading (b) from 3.93 to 5.51 (rho 1.0).

outcomes.statement: For pairs of neurons in the same cNE, spike train PWCs were much narrower than the PWCs of their STRFs' temporal profiles, while for pairs not in the same cNE the spike train PWCs were often as wide as the STRF PWCs.
outcomes.source: Results, Synchrony between cNE members cannot be fully explained by receptive field overlap, paragraph 1; Figure 6A to F
outcomes.quote: Comparing STRF PWCs to spike train PWCs ( Figure 6A–6F ) revealed that the spike train PWCs ( Figure 6C , histogram) were much narrower than the STRF PWCs ( Figure 6C , solid line) for neuronal pairs within the same cNE. In contrast, for non-cNE pairs, the spike train PWCs were often as wide as the STRF PWCs
outcomes.notes: Assumed, the STRF PWC (cross-correlation of the two temporal profiles) made non-negative by subtracting its minimum (ii), as the Results call STRF PWCs 'broad' and non-cNE spike PWCs 'often as wide as' them (Synchrony between cNE members, paragraph 1; cNE events are not fully accounted for by stimulus synchronization, paragraph 5). Then the spike PWC (+-50 ms) is sharper than the STRF PWC in 62.8% of 1012 cNE pairs and 43.2% of non-cNE pairs, and the spike/STRF sharpness ratio is lower for cNE pairs (median 0.800 against 1.077, Mann-Whitney p = 1.3e-53). Taking the absolute value (iii) or dividing by the number of overlapping lags before subtracting the minimum (iv, which removes the taper of a finite cross-correlation) agree, with 58.4% and 76.2% of cNE pairs sharper and p = 4.1e-76 and 1.1e-39; with a baseline subtracted from the spike PWCs, 87.9 to 95.8% under (ii) to (iv). With negative values set to zero (i), the STRF PWCs are 4 ms wide, no wider than the spike PWC in 97.4% of non-cNE pairs, and spike PWCs are sharper in only 6.9% of cNE pairs (27.7 to 34.3% with a baseline subtracted), though the ratio is still lower for cNE pairs (p = 3.3e-61). The spike PWC sharpness on the raw +-50 ms histogram is itself off the paper's scale (median 12 ms for cNE pairs against about 2; fig6-member-pwc-sharpness-delay), so the comparison is between two measures that both differ from the paper's. Question for the authors, how the STRF PWC was computed and compared (recorded as a finding).
deviations: cNE detection details the paper does not fix are this attempt's readings, from the claims file's opening comment and cne.py (Marcenko-Pastur bound (1 + sqrt(n/T))^2, symmetric fastICA with logcosh, sign reading (a) for membership, spikes inside the stimulus period only).
STRFs for the temporal profiles at 1 ms with 50 lags, the data set's sample code's 50 ms; profile = mean over frequency of the STRF minus its mean (Figure 6B, E legend).

Assumption, the STRF PWC is made non-negative by subtracting its minimum; the paper does not say. Absolute value and overlap-normalised readings agree; negative values set to zero gives the opposite result on the first part of the criterion.
PWCs use the spikes inside the stimulus period, on the stimulus clock.

outcomes.statement: In every penetration, spike train PWCs were significantly sharper (narrower) for pairs of neurons in the same cNE than for pairs not in the same cNE.
outcomes.source: Results, Synchrony between cNE members cannot be fully explained by receptive field overlap, paragraph 2; Figure 6J; Figure 6-figure supplement 1; Supplementary file 1
outcomes.quote: The PWCs were significantly narrower for cNE pairs than for non-cNE pairs (p < 0.001, Mann-Whitney U test; Figure 6J ; see Figure 6-figure supplement 1 for each of the other penetrations)
outcomes.notes: With +-50 ms lags, cNE pairs have sharper PWCs at p < 0.001 in 14 of 16 recordings; the exceptions are site 5 (5 cNE pairs, p = 0.023) and site 6 (10 pairs, p = 0.074), where cNE pairs are still sharper in median. With +-100 ms, 12 of 16. Over all recordings there are 1012 cNE and 13162 non-cNE pairs, against the paper's 3087 and 8838; the paper's per-recording cNE pair counts are larger than the cNE sizes it reports allow if each pair is counted once, so it may count pairs differently. Its total of 11925 pairs suggests that non-cNE pairs are pairs of two cNE members; this is asked of a reader (questions/see-2018.yaml). With the non-cNE pairs so restricted (5728 pairs) the result is the same, 14 and 12 of 16. With a baseline subtracted from the PWCs (variants the claims file does not name), 11 to 14 of 16.
deviations: cNE detection details the paper does not fix are this attempt's readings, from the claims file's opening comment and cne.py (Marcenko-Pastur bound (1 + sqrt(n/T))^2, symmetric fastICA with logcosh, sign reading (a) for membership, spikes inside the stimulus period only).
PWC lag bins of 1 ms over +-50 and +-100 ms, the claims file's readings; the paper does not fix them.
PWCs use the spikes inside the stimulus period, on the stimulus clock.

outcomes.statement: PWCs between members of the same cNE are sharp, with a median sharpness of about 2 ms, a mean sharpness of 3.39 +/- 1.21 ms and a mean absolute peak delay of 0.76 +/- 1.74 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, Synchrony between cNE members cannot be fully explained by receptive field overlap, paragraph 2; Results, cNE events are not fully accounted for by stimulus synchronization, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: The median PWC sharpness for member neurons was ~2 ms ... since PWCs between pairs of neurons in the same cNE are sharp, with mean sharpness values of 3.39 ± 1.21 ms ( Figure 6G–6J , Figure 6-figure supplement 1 ), and mean absolute peak delays of 0.76 ± 1.74 ms
outcomes.notes: Pooled over 1012 cNE pairs (+-50 ms; given as measured), the median sharpness is 12.0 ms and the mean 12.52 +/- 5.88 ms, against about 2 and 3.39 +/- 1.21 ms; the mean absolute peak delay 1.82 ms is within 0.76 +/- 1.74 ms. Per recording 12.2, 12.5 and 1.54 ms; with +-100 ms the sharpness is about 33 ms. One of three values holds. 80% of cNE pairs peak at 0 or 1 ms; the half-count width of a raw histogram includes its flat base (a flat histogram gives 25 ms over +-50 ms). With a baseline subtracted (the count expected from the two rates, or the mean of the outer lags; variants the claims file does not name) the median is 6 to 16 ms, and over +-20 ms it is 6 ms. Only a +-10 ms window gives 3 ms (mean 3.11), where a flat histogram gives 5 ms, so the window sets the value; even there the median is outside 2 +/- 0.2 ms. The lag range and baseline handling are a question for the authors (recorded as a finding).
deviations: cNE detection details the paper does not fix are this attempt's readings, from the claims file's opening comment and cne.py (Marcenko-Pastur bound (1 + sqrt(n/T))^2, symmetric fastICA with logcosh, sign reading (a) for membership, spikes inside the stimulus period only).
PWC lag bins of 1 ms over +-50 and +-100 ms, the claims file's readings; the paper does not fix them.
PWCs use the spikes inside the stimulus period, on the stimulus clock.

outcomes.statement: Across 16 penetrations, 104 cNEs were identified from 655 isolated neurons, an average of 6.5 +/- 2.0 cNEs per penetration.
outcomes.source: Results, cNEs are not depth-biased and reflect local circuitry, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Across 16 penetrations, we identified a total of 104 cNEs ... The average number of cNEs per penetration was 6.5 ± 2.0
outcomes.notes: 16 recordings and 655 units, the paper's counts, one file per penetration and stimulus. 104 cNEs, 6.50 +/- 1.97 per recording (range 3 to 10). Each recording has one stimulus file, so the reading of which file was used does not arise.

outcomes.statement: The number of cNEs per penetration increased with the number of isolated neurons (R2 = 0.74), and was about 15% of the number of recorded neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, cNEs are not depth-biased and reflect local circuitry, paragraph 1; Figure 7A; Supplementary file 1
outcomes.quote: For each penetration, the number of cNEs was ~15% of the recorded number of neurons ... the covariance between the number of identified cNEs and the number of isolated neurons ( Figure 7A ; R 2 = 0.74)
outcomes.notes: Slope 0.140 cNEs per unit, R2 0.745, F-test p = 1.7e-05 (paper 0.74, p = 1.68e-5). The fraction is 16.1% (a, given as measured), 14.0% (b) and 15.9% (c), all within tolerance.

outcomes.statement: The mean cNE size was 7.4 +/- 2.5 neurons, about 17% of the recorded neurons, and increased with the number of isolated neurons, more weakly than the number of cNEs (R2 = 0.33).
outcomes.source: Results, cNEs are not depth-biased and reflect local circuitry, paragraph 1; Figure 7B; Supplementary file 1
outcomes.quote: The mean number of neurons in cNEs was 7.4 ± 2.5 neurons. This again depended on the number of isolated neurons ( Figure 7B ), with mean cNE size ~17% of the total number of recorded neurons in the column. However, the covariance between mean cNE size and the number of isolated neurons ( Figure 7B ; R 2 = 0.33) was not as strong
outcomes.notes: Mean size 4.58 +/- 1.84 pooled over 104 cNEs (given as measured) and 4.34 per recording, against 7.4 +/- 2.5; 10.7% of the units against 17%; per-recording mean size on units R2 0.807 (slope 0.078, p = 2.3e-06), against 0.33. Only the positive slope with p < 0.05 holds. Sign reading (b) gives a mean of 4.74 and R2 0.738. The cNEs are smaller than the paper's while their number matches, which points at the membership threshold or IC scaling (a question for the authors).

outcomes.quote: The IC weight of the vast majority of cNE member neurons was positive ... However, 9 cNEs (8.3%) also contained at least one neuron with a negative weight
outcomes.notes: Under sign reading (a), 24 of 104 cNEs (23.1%) have a member below the lower threshold, against 9; 90.8% of member weights are positive. Under reading (b), 65.

outcomes.notes: Under sign reading (a) (given as measured), 59.2% of 655 units are in one cNE, 34.4% in none and 6.4% in more than one; under (b), 61.2%, 32.1% and 6.7%. None is within tolerance (68, 9 and 23%).

outcomes.notes: 88.5% of 1025 member pairs counted once per cNE (88.3% of 1012 unique pairs) are under 200 um apart, by depth difference and Euclidean distance alike; per recording 61.4 to 100%.

outcomes.statement: cNE STRFs had stronger excitatory and inhibitory subfields than those of their member neurons, with a higher peak-trough difference.
outcomes.source: Results, cNEs show enhanced information processing, paragraph 4; Figure 10B; Supplementary file 1

outcomes.notes: Over 476 cNE and member pairs (the paper has 703, its cNEs being larger), cNE STRFs have a higher PTD under all four readings, signed-rank p = 8.0e-12 (linear projection, every bin above threshold), 3.8e-09 (linear, peak per run), 5.6e-04 (quadratic, every bin) and 2.4e-05 (quadratic, peak); cNE higher in 54 to 62% of pairs.

outcomes.statement: Surrogate spike trains from the 'shuffled' and 'preserved receptive field' (PR) models gave fewer cNEs than the real data, while the dichotomized Gaussian (DG) model gave more.
outcomes.source: Results, cNE events are not fully accounted for by stimulus synchronization, paragraph 6; Figure 11C; Supplementary file 1
outcomes.quote: Surrogate spike trains from the ‘shuffled’ and ‘PR’ models had significantly fewer cNEs ( Figure 11C ) than the real data. On the other hand, the ‘DG’ model overestimates the number of detected cNEs
outcomes.notes: Mean over 200 runs per recording; real 6.50 cNEs. Shuffled 0.23 and PR 1.41 (10-ms bins) or 1.52 (5-ms bins), fewer in all 16 recordings; DG 8.01, more in 15. Bonferroni (x3) paired t-test p = 4.6e-09, 3.0e-08 or 4.5e-08, and 1.6e-04, under both PR readings. The DG fit needed its latent correlation matrix made positive definite in 15 recordings (smallest eigenvalue down to -1.97; latent correlations changed by up to 0.56). A sampled run has 5-ms covariances correlated 0.977 to 0.999 with the real ones and rates within 0.0018, but the slope of its covariances on the real ones runs from 0.672 to 1.02, so at sites 1 and 16 (0.672 and 0.688) it under-reproduces the covariances by about a third. The PR model drops 18 to 61 spikes per recording, those in the first 100 ms.

findings.statement: The data set holds the 16 columnar recordings made with the 10-min DMR and RN (Figures 1 to 7, 10 and 11C to F). It does not hold the 50 repeats of the 5-s segments (Figure 9 and its supplements), the 15 repeats of the 10-min RN (Figure 11A, B and the 'repeat' coincidence ratios) or the eight 64-channel recordings with spontaneous and evoked epochs (Figure 8), although the paper's data availability statement points to this data set for its data.

The descriptor does not say that rn1 is the dynamic moving ripple and rn16 the ripple noise (the paper's names), that `position` is a pair of a lateral offset and a depth below the surface in um, or whether files with the same tip depth (sites 1 and 2, 3 and 4, and so on) are one penetration recorded with both stimuli. Their units were sorted separately and cannot be matched.

Two units have spike times out of order, site 4 unit 17 (1 step back of 0.03 ms, 8 repeated times) and site 7 unit 21 (28 steps back of up to 0.09 ms, 107 repeated times), against sorted times in the other 653.

disagreements.reason: The size ratio is lower for cNE pairs under both variants. "Spike PWC sharper in more than half of cNE pairs" holds only with minimum subtraction (63.2%) and fails with clipping (6.5%); both variants are the author's own. np.correlate on 50-lag profiles tapers to zero at +-49 ms by construction, so the STRF PWC sharpness reflects that taper and the offset more than the profiles, and it is compared with the window-dominated spike sharpness.

Reproduced (fragile). It passes only under linear projection with event reading (a), p = 5.4e-4 with cNE MI higher in 55.7% of pairs; the other three readings give p from 0.008 to 0.12. It passes on 1 of 4 readings with no seed check, and the same no-held-out MI bias applies, so the verdict is reproduced by the letter of the criterion but is not robust.

disagreements.reason: In this execution the linear projection with event reading (a) gives p = 0.00153 (cell 79), above the 0.001 bound; the other three readings give 0.0076, 0.049 and 0.185, so none passes. Across all five subsampling draws the reading passes in 2. The held-out MI passes clearly (p <= 1.6e-8), but the criterion asks for the in-sample MI. On the printed output the outcome is not_reproduced. Choosing the linear projection because it is the reading that passes is also a weak basis for the assumption. The stated p-values, seed results and percentages were written from an earlier execution, and the result changes from one execution to the next with fixed seeds, which the record does not mention.

paper_notes.statement: Not fixed by the paper; a question for its authors, so that they can confirm or correct the choice. How IC weights were scaled and membership thresholds set. With the Methods' detection, the number of cNEs matches the paper (104, 6.5 per recording, R2 0.745 against units), but the cNEs are smaller (4.6 against 7.4 members), 34% of units belong to none (paper 9%) and 24 cNEs have a negative member (paper 9).

Not fixed by the paper; a question for its authors, so that they can confirm or correct the choice. The lag bin, lag range and any baseline correction of the pairwise correlation functions. The half-count width of a 1-ms histogram over +-50 ms gives a median of 12 ms for cNE pairs, not about 2 ms, and the R2 against the correlation coefficient is 0.1 to 0.25, not about 0.5. Subtracting a baseline gives medians of 6 to 16 ms; only a window of +-10 ms, which by itself gives 5 ms for a flat histogram, comes near (3 ms).

Not fixed by the paper; a question for its authors, so that they can confirm or correct the choice. The STRF window and resolution, the MI projection bins, and how cNE events are timed for STRFs. With 5-ms bins and 20 lags (the data set's sample code), STRF MI over bin sizes peaks at 35 ms or 2 ms depending on how the 5000 events are taken, not at 10 to 15 ms, and cNE STRF MI exceeds member MI at p < 0.001 under no reading in the main subsampling draw and under the linear projection in 2 of 5 draws. Whether the STRF was estimated on events held out from the MI; with held-out events the MI is about a tenth to a fifth as large (event reading a) and cNE MI exceeds member MI under every reading.

Not fixed by the paper; a question for its authors, so that they can confirm or correct the choice. How the STRF PWC of Figure 6 was computed and how its sharpness was measured, given that a cross-correlation of temporal profiles has negative values. Subtracting its minimum (assumed here) makes spike PWCs sharper for 63% of cNE pairs; clipping at zero makes the STRF PWCs 4 ms wide and reverses this. Also the time bin of the PR model (5 ms assumed; 10 ms gives a median STRF similarity of 0.645, not 0.74).

The per-recording cNE pair counts in Supplementary file 1 (Figure 6J and its supplement, 3087 cNE pairs in all) exceed the number of member pairs the reported cNE sizes allow if each pair is counted once (for example 365 cNE pairs in a recording), so the paper may count cNE pairs per ordered pair or per cNE; this attempt finds 1012 unique pairs. Their total (11925) is below the 14174 pairs of all units, which suggests non-cNE pairs are pairs of two cNE members (asked of a reader in questions/see-2018.yaml).

entries.name: see-2018
entries.title: Coordinated neuronal ensembles in rat auditory cortex columns (See et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of See, Atencio, Sohal and Schreiner (2018) on CRCNS ac-3, which holds the 16 columnar recordings (655 units) made with the 10-min DMR and RN stimuli, and the stimuli. It detects coordinated neuronal ensembles (cNEs) by PCA and ICA and tests their number, size, membership, depth, stability, pairwise correlation functions, bin size dependence, STRFs, and comparison with surrogate models. The 5-s repeats, the 15 repeats of the 10-min RN and the 64-channel recordings are not in the data set.
